title: Isandro and the Choir
premise: Felix Reyes, the king's food-taster, has spent his life in a valley where magic cannot enter — until a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, and Felix discovers he alone can understand it. The child is the last voice of the Choir, a covenant of singers who once held two realms in balance, and its breaking has unleashed an endless winter from the other side. Guided by the child and hunted by those who broke the covenant, Felix must cross into the magical realm he was born shielded from, learn why his immunity to poison made him immune to magic's erasure, and reforge the Choir with his own untrained voice. In the end, Felix sacrifices his memories of the valley to become the covenant's living keystone, sealing the realms together as spring finally returns.
about_author: Sable Fairweather is the pen name of a former choir singer turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk songs in remote mountain valleys. Their fiction blends liturgical rhythm with kitchen-table intimacy, exploring what ordinary people owe to histories they never chose.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet him mid-service, tasting the king's soup and cataloguing flavors like prayers, established in his small, safe valley where nothing strange survives. That night, a knock: a child stands in the snow, barefoot, humming a melody that makes Felix's teeth ache. Emotional beat: quiet contentment cracked open by wonder.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The child cannot speak any known tongue, yet Felix understands her humming as words — names, warnings, the word 'winter' repeated like a bell. He hides her in the taster's quarters while palace scholars fail to place her language. Emotional beat: growing intimacy and dread as Felix realizes understanding her is itself impossible.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Researching valley records, Felix learns the border was drawn deliberately: magic was exiled here generations ago, and 'tasters' were originally covenant-wardens. The child's humming sharpens; frost creeps indoors wherever she sleeps. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your whole life is a wall built around you.

chapters.title: The King's Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Felix and Lord Cassian, the royal spymaster. Cassian knows what the child is and wants her silenced before the winter's source is traced to the crown's ancestors, who murdered the Choir to seize both realms. Felix smuggles the child out through the kitchens. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal on both sides.

chapters.title: Crossing the Salt Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the valley's edge, Felix steps over the boundary expecting death or madness — instead the child's song holds him together, and he feels magic recognize him like an old scar. They enter a realm of frozen cathedrals and singing ice. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the frozen cathedral they find the Choir's remnants: stone singers, mouths open mid-note, and one living member — an ancient woman, Maerlin, who remembers everything except why she stopped singing. She teaches Felix that the covenant requires voices freely given, not inherited. Emotional beat: grief for beauty abandoned.

chapters.title: Cassian's Winter
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Pursuing them across the border, Cassian reveals his own history: he was a Choir child sold to the crown, taught to hate the covenant that abandoned him. He offers Felix a bargain — return the child, keep your memories, let winter finish. Emotional beat: villainy rendered as wounded, reasonable despair.

chapters.title: The Price of a Voice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Maerlin dies completing the first verse of the reforging rite, passing Felix her fragment of the covenant-song. To sing it whole, Felix must feed the song his own memories — every taste, every face of the valley. He begins, losing his mother's name first. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: The Long Note
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, climax. On the cathedral steps, Felix sings the full covenant while Cassian attacks and the child joins with the voice she'd been saving all along. The song demands everything; Felix forgets the valley entirely even as the ice breaks and spring floods both realms. Cassian, hearing the note he was stolen from, lowers his blade and weeps. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: Spring, Unremembered
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, resolution. Felix wakes in the valley as a stranger to it, employed again as taster, with no memory of why the child now lives in the palace as the king's honored ward — only a melody he hums without knowing its name. The child smiles at him across the hall. Some covenants outlive memory. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, identity remade rather than restored.
